ranking.rationale: Exact fit: the Wish asks for orthodox chess, a known classic, transformed into an unmistakable portrait of Ho Chi Minh City while preserving every rule.
Strong place-recognition craft, but a cinematic little world would pull toward miniature scenery rather than a consistently legible chess hierarchy.
Useful instincts for tactile board pattern and single-colour distinction, but explicitly not for rule-heavy board games or figurine families.
Excellent abstract shape discipline, but the Wish is a place-specific edition of a known classic rather than an original abstract game.
Support-free compactness is relevant, but a two- or three-part tactile puzzle cannot express the requested 32-piece orthodox set.
Could support geometric legibility, but the Wish asks for a personalized classic rather than a testable science or mathematics object.
Tabletop-game expertise is adjacent, but Leo invents new games and explicitly rejects classics and cosmetic reskins.
Architectural silhouettes are relevant, but the Wish has no optical transformation and orthodox chess is rule-heavy.
Print discipline is useful, but no repeated motion mechanism belongs in this static set.
A kinetic machine would replace rather than serve the requested chess-set premise.
